fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single access point with a clearly visible address sign readable from the access road approach.

• Post a site map at the access point showing building locations, the internal drive aisle route, and the service area.

• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach both the main building and secondary building.

• Mark the secondary building with its own visible identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main building on arrival.

• Keep the dumpster enclosure clear of the drive aisle to avoid blocking emergency vehicle movement between structures.

• Trim vegetation along the internal drive aisle to maintain overhead and side clearance for emergency vehicles.

• Identify and mark any foot path or walkway providing rear access to both structures, so responders can reach the limited rear access area on foot if vehicles cannot.

• Keep the service area accessible and clearly marked so responders can use it as a staging area when the vehicle parking area is occupied.

• Post the physical address on both the main building and secondary building on the sides visible from the drive aisle.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin the tree cluster nearest to the building to reduce the amount of vegetation directly adjacent to the structure.

• Trim branches on scattered trees that extend close to the building roofline or walls.

• Keep the vegetation growing near the building walls trimmed back and separated from the structure.

• Maintain the grass cover around the building at a short, mowed height, particularly in areas between the tree clusters and the building.

• Keep the large paved area and open paved areas clear of dead leaves, dry grass, and plant debris that can accumulate and ignite.

• Clear vegetation, debris, and any encroaching plant growth from the rear of the building to improve access for firefighters and emergency vehicles.
